observations: A blocky rectangular head sits centered against a flat blue background with dark teal and pink vertical forms at the edges; two large circular eye shapes with crossed and striped fill dominate the upper face.
The mouth spans nearly the full width of the lower face, showing two rows of white rectangular teeth separated by a dark gap, outlined in red and black with a squared-off jaw beneath.
Dense overlapping lines in red, yellow, green, pink, and white run across the entire face surface; three stacked white rectangles appear on each cheek, distinct from the surrounding line work.
reading: The face reads more as mask than skin—its circular eyes crossed and striped, its mouth baring two full rows of teeth with a visible dark gap between them. Dense colored lines cover every surface without resolving into shadow or volume, keeping the form flat and loud at once. The white cheek marks sit apart from the surrounding tangle, functioning as notation rather than anatomy. The mood could be alarm or glee; the image holds both without settling.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #41 and #43. Where #41 builds its face from short overlapping strokes on a warm ground, #42 uses a flat blue field and hard circular eye forms, giving the face a more mask-like structure.

connections.reason: Both #42 and #43 place a blocky face against the same flat blue ground, but #43 tilts and stacks its features into horizontal slabs while #42 keeps the face upright and symmetrical with circular eye forms.

#41 and #42 both layer multicolored lines over a face shape, but #41 uses short directional strokes that blend into the surface, while #42 uses longer looping lines that stay visibly separate from the flat blue-filled form beneath.

lookingQuestion: What do the three stacked white rectangles on each cheek do to your reading of the face—do they read as part of the face structure, or as marks laid on top of it?
